title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
abstract: arXiv:2610.02188v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) trains a few-step student from the difference between separately estimated target and student scores, so it must keep an auxiliary diffusion model fitted to the student's evolving distribution at extra memory and computation cost. We introduce DMAD, Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation, which recasts distribution matching as classification and learns the required log-density ratios directly. Two discriminator heads on a shared backbone distinguish real data and teacher samples from the student's, and linear losses on their logits train the student without auxiliary score fitting. We prove that at the discriminator optimum these losses recover the distribution-matching gradient underlying DMD, through the classical identity linking discriminator logits to log-density ratios. We further introduce gap-based reweighting, which adapts teacher supervision across noise levels from the real

translated_title: DMAD：将分布匹配作为对抗蒸馏以实现快速视觉生成
translated_abstract: 分布匹配蒸馏通过分别估计的目标分数与学生分数之差来训练少步数学生模型，因此必须保留一个辅助扩散模型来拟合学生不断演化的分布，这带来了额外的内存和计算开销。我们提出DMAD（分布匹配作为对抗蒸馏），它将分布匹配重新表述为分类问题，并直接学习所需的Log密度比。共享骨干网络上的两个判别器头用于区分真实数据、教师样本与学生样本，通过对数几率上的线性损失即可训练学生模型，无需辅助分数拟合。我们证明，在判别器达到最优时，这些损失通过将判别器对数几率与Log密度比相联系的经典恒等式，恰好恢复了DMD背后的分布匹配梯度。我们进一步引入基于差距的重加权方法，可根据...（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: DMAD将分布匹配蒸馏重新表述为分类问题，利用共享骨干网络上的双判别器头直接学习Log密度比，无需辅助扩散模型即可训练少步学生模型，从而大幅降低内存与计算开销。
en_tdlr: DMAD recasts distribution matching as a classification problem, using two discriminator heads on a shared backbone to directly learn log-density ratios, eliminating the need for an auxiliary diffusion model in few-step distillation and thus reducing memory and computation costs.
